findings.claim: The A/B command reports DAT and exits 0 when either full run exits nonzero after printing healthy output. Only the light-run exit status participates in dat.

evidence.observed: control, base_rc42, head_rc42 each return ab_rc 0 and KET_LUAN_AB: DAT (9/9 phep dung). Fault injection replaces chay_bo return values; actual clone/import/comparator paths execute, with base=H to isolate return-code handling. No second full suite executed.

suggested_fix.where: lenh_ab, after all three process results; status belongs to the command runner, not to the nine independent semantic comparisons.
suggested_fix.how: Require rc 0 for base/day_du, H/day_du and H/nhe before reporting DAT; preserve nonzero rc and diagnostics.
suggested_fix.locking_test: Inject rc 42 after positive output separately at each of the three run boundaries; each must make the command fail, with an rc-0 control. A mutant dropping each rc check must fail its matching test.
suggested_fix.new_risks: Do not fold process status into unrelated comparison predicates or misclassify valid stricter A+3 outcomes.

findings.claim: The oversized-file vector is invalid JSON, so it does not test the 65,536-byte guard. Removing that guard leaves c82 green while a valid 65,537-byte result is accepted.

evidence.observed: CASE audit_bo c82 rc 0; CASE no_size_limit c82 rc 0. LARGE_VALID_JSON 65537: H infrastructure_error, mutant hoan_tat. Mutation replaces the conditional decode/size rejection with unconditional UTF-8 decoding. A second mutant f.read(65537)->f.read(65536) also survives c82. Replacing only the oversized vector with valid padded JSON preserves H rc0 and kills both mutants with rc3 / DO:c82 vector 28 (extra_probes.log). Direct boundary control: 65536 bytes => hoan_tat; 65537 => infrastructure_error on H (boundary-control.json).

suggested_fix.where: c82 VEC and the K5a test-mutant catalog; the production size check itself currently works.
suggested_fix.how: Add syntactically valid result JSON padded with whitespace to 65,536 and 65,537 bytes, with all identity/type/triple checks otherwise valid, plus a distinct size-check mutant.
suggested_fix.locking_test: Both parent runners accept the within-limit control and reject the oversized input; removing the byte limit must produce rc 3 / DO:c82, not an unrelated parse exception.
suggested_fix.new_risks: Keep bytes rather than Unicode-character length as the unit; avoid a truncated JSON vector that another guard also rejects.

findings.claim: chay_quan_sat catches TimeoutExpired and discards the Popen handle without terminating or reaping the child. A timed-out measurement can keep running and writing after the function reports failure and its temporary hook directory is removed.

evidence.observed: timeout=.15: function returned (None,None,LOI_CHAY: TimeoutExpired) after 0.158 s; the real child then wrote timeout-after-return after sleeping .4 s. TIMEOUT_CHILD_CONTINUED True. Harmless probe naturally exited; no lingering reviewer child.

suggested_fix.where: chay_quan_sat, which owns the process and timeout; do_cay cannot clean up the discarded handle.
suggested_fix.how: On timeout, terminate the owned process tree using a bounded cleanup strategy and reap it before returning KHONG_DO_DUOC. Preserve captured output and the actual timeout reason.
suggested_fix.locking_test: A real child (and a descendant) schedules a marker after the deadline; the helper must return failure and no marker may appear after cleanup. Keep a healthy process control and a mutant that omits cleanup.
suggested_fix.new_risks: Do not kill unrelated process groups; make ownership explicit and keep cleanup bounded if termination fails.

findings.claim: A direct Python child whose executable is a renamed copy is omitted from python_con. It can run -I and read a tracked out-of-zone file while the measurement reports SACH with 0 children / 0 hook starts. This also falsifies r14 Acceptance 4's remaining positive claim about the total number of Python children; the accepted surplus-hook/shell/native limits do not cover this zero-surplus direct-child counterexample.

evidence.observed: Standard interpreter -I: rc0, python_con=1, bat_dau_con=0 => KHONG_DO_DUOC. Renamed byte-for-byte interpreter -I: rc0, python_con=0, bat_dau_con=0 => SACH, though child reads CONTEXT.md. Same renamed interpreter without -I: rc0, hook records CONTEXT.md => NGOAI_VUNG. Parent reads the required ops/ci_provenance.py witness in all three cases. Reusing tu_kiem_vung with only the child executable changed to this copied interpreter gives 107/116: all nine -I/-S/-E × three-operation inputs incorrectly return SACH. See alias_matrix.py and alias_matrix.log.

suggested_fix.where: la_python/doc_log and the positive assurance sentence in frozen spec r14 Acceptance 4; all three vung operations share this classifier.
suggested_fix.how: Do not claim all Python launches from filename matching. Conservatively classify unknown executables as not measured unless positively known outside the measured class, or obtain a new explicit owner-approved limitation narrowing the guarantee to recognized interpreter launches. An expanded regex alone does not close the class; the already-planned OS-level successor is the stronger remedy.
suggested_fix.locking_test: Run a renamed/copied interpreter with -I, -S and -E as the sole child for each operation. It must not yield SACH; keep normal-interpreter and hooked-renamed controls. Preserve the separately accepted aggregate-surplus limitation.
suggested_fix.new_risks: Conservative classification may reject valid native tools; widening the regex can create false confidence. Any further assurance reduction needs explicit authority and must not be recorded as a code fix of the inherited class.
